stories.title: Norway's Newest Marine Protected Area Shelters Rich Marine Habitat, Whales, and Seabirds
stories.label: ocean
stories.summary: Norway just created a huge new protected area in the ocean called Andfjorden, covering about 714 square miles of sea. That's roughly the size of 260,000 football pitches, all now safeguarded for whales, seabirds, and a wonderfully rich mix of marine life living both above and below the water. The government made this official on September 18th, so it's already law and already protecting these waters. It's a real, lasting win for one of the planet's most beautiful and biodiverse coastlines.
stories.why_good: A government took concrete, finalized action to permanently protect a huge stretch of ocean habitat for whales and seabirds -- not a proposal or study, but an established protected area.

stories.title: A Strategy of Cash-for-Photos Turns Animal Hunters into Animal Protectors in Indonesia
stories.label: animals
stories.summary: On the island of Borneo, people who used to hunt endangered birds and orangutans are now getting paid to photograph them instead. Nine villages in Indonesia's West Kalimantan province have joined a pay-per-picture program that gives families extra income for protecting wildlife rather than harming it. The shift has turned former hunters into some of the animals' biggest defenders, since a living creature is now worth more to them than a dead one. It's a simple, clever way to align people's livelihoods with conservation, and it's already making a real difference on the ground.
stories.why_good: A real, working program that turned hunters into protectors and is measurably helping endangered species survive.
